children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures shot up by mid-session Tuesday, gleaning support from strong increases in crude oil and the Chicago soy complex.
Additional support came from upticks in European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil.

Close to session highs An analyst said canola was pushing close to its session highs, noting "there's a lot of uncertainty in the market." After speaking with a number of farmers, the analyst said "they are mystified as to what canola is" given the range of crop conditions across the Prairies.
With the canola harvest still in its early stages, the provincial crop reports have said little, if anything substantial, about yields.
Also, Statistics Canada no longer issues its August production estimates, with its first report on this year's crops scheduled for Sept. 16.
Such a follower The analyst said he hopes canola doesn't fall below $800 per tonne during harvest, but the oilseed could drop to $750. He said a lot is predicated on crude oil prices.
"Canola is such a follower," he said.
The Canadian dollar turned lower with the loonie slipping to 71.95 U.S. cents late Tuesday morning, compared to Monday's close of 72.12.
